criteria.evidence: Out: for a domain id, the list of business intents that touch it and the capabilities in it (and, through those, their functionalities), each with its page link.  /  Rules: "The search still returns the link from the side that holds it, marked \"one-sided\"." and "the search reports it as \"not in the spine\"."  /  Inputs: "shows the mark beside it"
criteria.fix: Make the search output in Inputs / Outputs carry the full shape the Rules section promises: each listed intent shows its Touches mark (adds, changes or removes) and a "one-sided" flag when the link is held on one side only, and a capability whose domain id is missing from the spine is listed as "not in the spine". Add the matching warning to the check's outputs (a capability naming a domain the spine does not hold). Then add Given/When/Then criteria for those two paths: a one-sided link is returned by the search marked "one-sided", and a capability naming an unknown domain id is reported as "not in the spine" with a warning, not an error.

criteria.evidence: A capability names at most one domain; a domain lists its capabilities only through those capability entries, so there is one place to change.  /  A domain is never a level of a plan tree, never a tracker issue, and never carries an ICE; any of these is an error, because domains set which areas the product covers, not what work is done.
Given a business intent whose Touches list names a domain that does not name it back in `intents`, when the check runs, then it warns, naming the intent and the domain, and still passes.

Parent: "In: the loose links from a domain to its business intents and capabilities, so a search by domain can be answered." Child: "The check finds a domain linked to a tracker issue by reading files only, never the tracker: a domain entry in the spine that carries an `issue` field ... or a node in a plan file whose `kind` is domain"

A domain lists the business intents and capabilities in it, so "which business intents serve the commerce domain?" can be answered. Domains are never in a plan or the tracker.  /  Out of scope: Deciding readiness — fn-724 owns it, and a domain plays no part in it.
